trigger: a caller holding only group-scoped ITServiceOwner (no fleet-wide ManagementGroup:Read) calls list_management_group_roles via MCP
summary: list_management_group_roles was missing REST's leading ManagementGroup:Read gate (#2376), letting a caller with only group-scoped ITServiceOwner read role grants via MCP where REST would 403. Fixed with the same leading gate plus a regression test.

trigger: any caller with ApiToken:Write RBAC calls create_api_token via a supervised or lower MCP tier
summary: create_api_token had no approval-gating and no MFA step-up, unlike every sibling write tool in this batch, with a changelog/comment falsely implying a compensating control existed (I6a false assurance). Fixed by adding ApiToken:Write to mcp_policy.hpp's supervised-tier requires_approval() list, closing the gap on both REST and MCP simultaneously via the shared policy table.

adjudication_rationale: architecture-wide gap, pre-existing, not scoped to this batch - explicit decision not to block this PR on an architectural fix outside its remit
waiver_rationale: architecture-wide root cause is out of scope for a tool-parity batch; tracked centrally on #4309 rather than fixed piecemeal per-PR at this point in the batch's history
summary: Cookie-session principals bypass MCP tier/approval enforcement entirely (mcp_tier is only ever set on an actual MCP token). Filed/tracked as #4309; NOT fixed in this round (superseded by pass_ordinal 2 below for the 3 highest-value tools in this same PR, and again at pass_ordinal 0 for 2 more).

trigger: an interactive (cookie) session with ordinary ApiToken:Write/Delete or UserManagement:Write RBAC calls create_api_token, revoke_api_token, or unlock_account via MCP
adjudicated_by: Dave (operator), via AskUserQuestion - chose to deny cookie sessions outright on these 3 tools rather than defer entirely to #4309
adjudication_rationale: raw credential-minting and account-lockout-clearing are high-value enough operations that the architecture-wide gap's usual defer-to-#4309 posture was judged insufficient for these 3 specifically
summary: 4 independent reviewers (unhappy-path, enterprise-readiness, compliance-officer, consistency-auditor) converged: a hijacked/CSRF'd dashboard session could self-mint a persistent credential, revoke any token, or clear an account lockout with NEITHER the MFA step-up nor the maker-checker approval ticket the REST twin enforces. Fixed with a session->mcp_tier.empty() deny-outright guard on exactly these 3 tools.

trigger: a caller sends a non-string parent_id/description/membership_type/scope_expression to create_management_group
summary: param_str() silently returns "" on a JSON type mismatch - a numeric parent_id created a top-level group instead of the intended child, with no error. update_management_group already had the correct is_string() pattern; applied to create_management_group too.

trigger: a caller sends a non-string mcp_tier to create_api_token
summary: param_str() silently defaults mcp_tier to "" on a type mismatch - the MOST PERMISSIVE token shape this store can mint (no tier restriction, no 90-day TTL cap). A type-mismatched mcp_tier must be rejected, never defaulted. Note (pass_ordinal 4 below): this specific check was later found to be defense-in-depth, since the #2405 C8 schema gate already catches the same mismatch for this approval-gated tool.

trigger: a reader of assign_management_group_role's served description or handler comment believes RbacStore::validate_assignment's dangerous-role-block chokepoint is what stops an engine-role assignment
summary: The described protection is actually unreachable (assign_role already rejects principal_type=="engine" before validate_assignment runs); the real protection is the F2 shadow-row guard. Corrected description and comment.
